- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots in next 5–7d; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; model often fails to revert; use 10–15d moving average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment history shows high volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with exponential decay (α=0.3) to reduce noise amplification.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to ignore policy/seasonal effects; add 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is bearish and events are frequent.
